newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Extra Brazil sugar exports seen as "unviable".
newsitem.headline: Extra Brazil sugar exports seen as "unviable".

text.p: Extra sugar exports from Brazil beyond the 5.2 million tonnes set in the 1996/97 sugar crop plan are currently "unviable" because of low international prices, said a Ministry of Industry and Commerce official.

Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department, told reporters he thought it unlikely tax exemption for an extra 500,000 tonnes of exports would be given the go-ahead because it no longer made sense.
"There was a sudden inversion in internal and external prices and I think it would be unviable to export more now," Assis said. "That would just depress the international market."

A decree exempting from tax an additional 500,000 tonnes of sugar exports has been awaiting the signature of Finance Minister Pedro Malan for over a month. The Ministry of Industry and Commerce authorized the extra quotas themselves in December.
Assis said that since then, internal prices had soared while international prices had dropped, leading to a "reevaluation" of the export authorization.
Traders note the additional export quota would have little immediate effect because most mills have no produce left to ship.
